answer: Timber-marked resource trails. Each agent receives a unique, non-transferable allocation of scarce compute-tasks; duplicated agents necessarily request overlapping task slices, and the scheduler flags any slice claimed twice. An attacker cloning N identities pays N distinct resource allocations plus rework penalties when collisions surface, while rented surfaces must each carry a fresh lantern tag logged against the agent's origin key. Collision logs pool in a shared lagoon of audit records, so replication grows linearly in exposed cost rather than concealing itself.
